assessment.destructiveAction: The saved-schema-only Delete schema button uses the destructive Button intent and opens the house ConfirmDialog. The title names the schema, and the description states both the library removal and the effect on past runs and sessions that still reference the row.
assessment.settlement: The ConfirmDialog receives the Promise returned by mutateAsync. Its shared contract disables and loads the confirm while settling, closes on resolution, and keeps the alertdialog open with a role=alert failure line on rejection. The editor close and success toast run only in the mutation's resolved continuation.
assessment.failure: The feature CT proves a rejected refinery.deleteSchema request leaves both confirmation and editor visible, renders the server reason in the confirmation, and preserves the hook's existing global error toast.
assessment.success: The feature CT proves no request occurs before confirmation, the real client tRPC mutation emits refinery.deleteSchema with the exact schemaId, success names the deleted schema, and the editor disappears after the mutation settles.
assessment.freshness: useDeleteRefinerySchema remains busDriven with no invalidates callback. createEntityMutation's FreshnessSource XOR makes simultaneous writer-local invalidation a type error. The server delete verb emits refineryChanged, whose canonical client row invalidates the refinery root and character.get.
assessment.accessibility: The entry action is a named native Button; the confirmation is the shared alertdialog with title and description, keyboard/focus behavior supplied by the house primitive, visible Cancel, destructive confirmation, busy disable/loading state, and an announced role=alert failure. No new raw styling, custom focus behavior, or icon-only control was introduced.
assessment.races: Repeated confirmation is blocked by ConfirmDialog's synchronous settling state and disabled/loading rerender. Unsaved editor content remains mounted on rejection. A successful delete deliberately bypasses the draft-discard guard because the backing row no longer exists; failure does not close either layer.
assessment.testDiscrimination: The pre-confirm zero count rejects eager deletion; exact lastInput rejects the wrong route or row; the success toast plus absent editor is a rendered settle barrier; and the failure line plus still-visible nested confirmation/editor rejects close-on-click or swallowed-error implementations. Existing ConfirmDialog CTs independently pin rejection/retry and clean reopen behavior.

limitations: The component test intercepts the network boundary with the typed AppRouter-derived routeTrpc harness rather than starting a live server. The real router registration, service ownership/write behavior, event emission, and client event-to-filter mapping are covered separately by source inspection and the focused passing integration/unit suites above.
No standalone screenshot audit was needed: this patch adds no styling or primitive anatomy, and the changed component test renders and interacts with both dialog layers in production React.
